title: Function and tool calling
summary: The model returns a tool call with JSON arguments, your code runs it, and you send the result back. Strict schemas, tool_choice and loop limits decide how reliable that cycle is.
useIf: The model must fetch data or take actions, and you need arguments that your code can trust.
avoidIf: A single structured answer is enough. A schema-constrained output needs no tool loop.

explain.md: You describe each **tool** with a name, a description and a JSON schema. The model never runs anything. It returns a `function_call` item (Responses) or a tool call (Chat) with arguments, **your application** executes it, and you return the result tagged with the `call_id`. The loop repeats until the model answers in text [[r9]].

explain.title: The tool-calling loop
explain.alt: The app sends messages and tool schemas to the model, which returns a tool call. The app runs the tool and returns the result to the model, which produces the final answer.
explain.src:
sequenceDiagram
  participant App
  participant Model
  participant Tool
  App->>Model: messages and tool schemas
  Model-->>App: tool call with arguments
  App->>Tool: run with arguments
  Tool-->>App: result or error
  App->>Model: result with call id
  Model-->>App: final answer

explain.caption: Controls (check date 2026-10-13)
head: Control
OpenAI
Anthropic
rows: `parallel_tool_calls: false` gives zero or one call
`strict: true` recommended. Chat stays non-strict by default
Forced `any` or `tool` returns 400 on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, and with manual extended thinking [[r50]]

explain.md: In Responses, omitting `strict` makes the API try to normalise the schema to strict and fall back to non-strict, which then shows `strict: false` [[r9]]. A fine-tuned model that makes several calls in one turn loses strict mode. **Custom tools** take free text instead of JSON. Definitions count as input tokens, the guide suggests fewer than 20 functions at the start of a turn, and `tool_search` with `defer_loading` loads large catalogs on demand on gpt-5.4 and later.

explain.title: Reasoning plus tools needs Responses on newer OpenAI models
explain.md: From GPT-5.4, Chat Completions does not support tool calling with `reasoning_effort` other than `none`. GPT-6 Astra and 6.1 Sol need Responses for tools, and Azure `gpt-5.6-sol` fails with "Function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported" even when you omit effort, because the default is `medium` [[r6]] [[r2]] [[r15]].

GPT-6 adds **async tool calling**: set `async: true` on a tool and the model keeps working while your application runs it. You return the result with the original `call_id`, and your application still runs the tool [[tr6]].

whereToUse: Retrieval from private systems, such as order status, tickets or inventory
Actions: create a ticket, send a message, update a record, with approval gates
Calculators and code execution for tasks models do poorly in text
Agent loops that plan, call tools and read results
Wrapping an internal API with a validated argument schema

use: The answer needs live data or a side effect
You can describe each tool with a clear schema and purpose
You can validate arguments and authorise inside the tool
avoid: Large catalogs loaded at once, which waste tokens and confuse selection
Letting the model decide authorisation, since tools must check permissions themselves
Unbounded loops with no iteration cap
flips: Catalog exceeds about 20 tools: use `tool_search` with `defer_loading` or a pre-selection step
Reasoning plus tools on a newer OpenAI model: use Responses
A tool takes minutes: use async tool calling or a task pattern

pitfalls.symptom: Arguments fail validation in some calls
pitfalls.cause: Strict mode is off, or a fine-tuned model lost it after multi-call turns
pitfalls.fix: Set `strict: true`, validate again in code and return errors as tool output

pitfalls.symptom: The model picks the wrong tool from a long list
pitfalls.cause: Many similar tools and long descriptions crowd the context
pitfalls.fix: Shrink the catalog, sharpen descriptions, or load tools on demand with `tool_search`

pitfalls.symptom: Forced tool choice returns 400 on a recent Claude model
pitfalls.cause: `any` and `tool` are not accepted on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1
pitfalls.fix: Use `auto` with a strict tool or structured outputs

pitfalls.symptom: The loop runs for dozens of calls
pitfalls.cause: No iteration cap and tool errors are swallowed
pitfalls.fix: Cap calls, return concise errors, and stop on repeated failures

scenarios.title: A catalog of 120 internal tools
scenarios.situation: An internal assistant exposes 120 tools. Selection errors rise and every request pays for the full list of definitions.
unknowns: How often are most tools unused?
Can tools be grouped by task?
scenarios.question: What do you change?

options.name: Use `tool_search` with `defer_loading` so only relevant tools are loaded per turn
options.why: It cuts input tokens and confusion, and the guide recommends it for large catalogs on gpt-5.4 and later [[r9]].
options.tradeoff: Adds a search step, and weak tool descriptions make search miss.

options.name: Send all 120 tools and lower temperature
options.why: Definitions stay in every request and temperature does not fix selection.
options.tradeoff: Passing every tool is fine for a catalog under about 20.

options.name: Pre-select a subset with your own retriever before each call
options.why: Works on any model and you control the logic.
options.tradeoff: You build and maintain the selector and its evals.

flips.then: Use your own pre-selection by task or embeddings.

scenarios.takeaway: Load only the tools a turn needs.

scenarios.title: Forcing structured behaviour on a recent Claude model
scenarios.situation: A workflow sets `tool_choice` to a named tool so the model always returns structured data. After moving to Claude Sonnet 5.5 every call returns 400.
unknowns: Is a tool needed at all, or only a typed answer?
scenarios.question: How do you fix it?

options.name: Retry with `tool_choice: any`
options.tradeoff: Forced choice still works on models that accept it.

options.name: Use `tool_choice: auto` with a strict tool, or structured outputs through `output_config.format`
options.why: No side effect is needed, so structured outputs give a typed answer with schema validity and no forced choice [[r50]] [[r32]].
options.tradeoff: You must design a schema and handle refusals.

options.name: Pin the old model to avoid the change
options.tradeoff: Defers the migration to a retirement date.

flips.if: A real tool call must run
flips.then: Keep `auto`, a strict tool and a clear description.
Use a model that accepts it, and document the dependency.

scenarios.takeaway: When no action is needed, use structured outputs, not a forced tool.

quiz.q: Order the steps of one tool-calling round trip.
items: App sends messages and tool schemas
Model returns a tool call with arguments
App returns the result with the call id
quiz.explain: The model only proposes calls. Your application executes them and returns results tagged with the call id before the model answers.

quiz.q: Azure `gpt-5.6-sol` fails with 'Function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported' even though the request omits effort. Why?
options: The default effort is `medium`, which Chat Completions cannot use with tools
The tool list is too long
quiz.explain: Omitting effort applies the model default of `medium`, and Chat Completions does not support tools with effort other than `none`. Use Responses or set effort to `none`.

quiz.q: Which practices keep tool calling safe?
options: Authorise inside each tool using the caller's identity
Trust the arguments because the schema is strict
Cap the number of tool calls
Return tool errors as text so the model can recover
quiz.explain: Tools must check permissions, loops need caps and errors should be returned. A strict schema ensures shape, not that the arguments are safe.

flashcards.front: What is the OpenAI guidance for the number of tools?
flashcards.back: Fewer than 20 functions at the start of a turn (soft advice). Use `tool_search` with `defer_loading` for large catalogs on gpt-5.4 and later.
